newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY EXPORT FINANCERS SAY '97 BUSINESS TO SURGE.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY EXPORT FINANCERS SAY '97 BUSINESS TO SURGE.

text.p: Hungary's government export insurer MEHIB and sister company Eximbank expect to multiply their business several times between 1996 and this year, their leaders told a professional conference on Friday.
"We are still young, but we have definitely moved out of infancy," said Balazs Botos, chief executive of insurer MEHIB Rt. "We are expecting dynamic growth."

Modelled on similar U.S. institutions, MEHIB and Eximbank were set up jointly in 1994 as part of a string of measures meant to halt a decline in exports caused by the collapse of the communist-era trading system.
MEHIB expects to double its political insurance coverage from 1996's 59 billion forints. The figure for 1995 was 25 billion, Botos said.
Some of the increase will come from exports to Russia and to the former Yugoslavia, which were recently placed on the list of countries for which MEHIB provides regular coverage, he added.

In commercial insurance, MEHIB expects a three-fold increase from last year's 4.5 billion forints coverage -- already a five-fold increase on 1995 -- despite growing competition from private insurers.
MEHIB's average political insurance rate is 2.4 percent of insured value, while its commercial insurance rate is 0.4 percent on the average, Botos said.

Eximbank expects direct export-lending to companies to increase to eight to 10 billion forints in 1997 compared to five billion last year and virtually zero in 1995, said Tamas Gyorgy, the head of Eximbank's controlling and economics departments.
Lending through commercial banks grew to about 27 billion forints in 1996 from 12 billion in 1995, with further growth expected in 1997, he said.

From a separate loaning scheme funded by the central budget and administered by Eximbank, Gyorgy said he expects Hungarian exporters to take up the full 50 billion forints available for 1997 after borrowing 95 percent of the 25 billion forints available last year.
